來源載明巴拉班管管身多用杏木，亦見榛木、梨木、桑木與黃楊木；另有記載稱可用桑木或: The sources state that the balaban's body is mostly apricot wood, and also hazel, pear, mulberry and boxwood; another account says harder woods such as mulberry or walnut may be used. The sound is produced by a large double reed made from a sedge that grows in arid regions, one end flattened and inserted into the top of the body. Outside the reed is an adjuster made from a willow or vine twig split lengthwise; there is also a cap to protect the reed, made of willow, hazel, dogwood or mulberry. The materials of the other parts are not stated in the sources.

巴拉班管屬氣鳴樂器，發聲分類為雙簧圓柱管。其音色偏暗、輕而弱，亦被描述為溫暖，多: The balaban is an aerophone, classed as a double-reed cylindrical pipe. Its tone is dark, light and weak, and also described as warm; it is mostly played in enclosed spaces and at indoor gatherings. The player keeps the sound continuous by circular breathing; the clip on the reed can be moved up and down to make the sound thinner or fuller, and to match an ensemble quickly. The body has eight fingerholes at the front and another at the back, and the pitch changes by opening and closing them, but the sources do not state the actual range. It is almost the same as the Turkish mey and the Armenian duduk, differing mainly in history and region; the flat-mouthpiece balaban sounds softer because its mouthpiece is flatter.
巴拉班管是氣鳴樂器，H-S 編號422.121-62，為圓筒形管身、雙簧的管樂器: The balaban is an aerophone, H-S 422.121-62, a cylindrical-bore, double-reed wind instrument, commonly with eight fingerholes and a thumbhole, the body mostly of apricot, mulberry and similar woods. The player stores air in the cheeks and breathes circularly, and can adjust the clip on the reed to change the timbre. It is popular in Azerbaijan, Iran and Turkey, and is used at weddings, festivals, pastoral songs, funerals and ashik music; traditionally two balabans and a percussionist play together.
巴拉班管見於亞塞拜然婚禮、節慶儀式，常由一名演奏者搭配打擊樂手；傳統合奏由兩名巴: The balaban appears at Azerbaijani weddings and festive ceremonies, often one player with a percussionist; the traditional ensemble is two balabans and a percussionist. It is also used for pastoral songs and funeral music, and to accompany songs in Turkmen and Kurdish cities such as Erbil, Sulaymaniyah and Kirkuk. Kamil Jalilov's balaban recording was included in the Voyager Golden Record and represents Azerbaijani mugham; the instrument is also used in ashik music.
巴拉班管起源於高加索，後被亞塞拜然音樂吸收，並見於亞塞拜然、伊朗與土耳其。193: The balaban originated in the Caucasus, was later absorbed into Azerbaijani music, and is found in Azerbaijan, Iran and Turkey. After the orchestra of Azerbaijani folk instruments was founded in 1931, it was used in that orchestra for the first time. It is also used to accompany songs in Turkmen and Kurdish cities such as Erbil, Sulaymaniyah and Kirkuk. Recordings of songs with Kamil Jalilov's balaban were included in the Voyager Golden Record, representing Azerbaijani mugham.
演奏時以手指覆蓋管身正面八孔與背面一孔，吹口端裝雙簧片，簧片上有夾箍，可上下推動: To play, cover the eight holes at the front of the body and the one at the back with the fingers; the double reed is fitted at the mouthpiece end, with a clip on the reed that is pushed up and down to make the tone thinner or fuller. The sound comes from the reed's vibration, and the player keeps it continuous with air held in the mouth while breathing in through the nose, a circular breathing common to Middle Eastern double-reed instruments. A beginner can first practise covering the holes and adjusting the clip, then gradually add circular breathing.
